name: Arah
overview: Arah is a male figure mentioned in the biblical record whose descendants played a role in the restoration of Judah after the Babylonian captivity. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is noted specifically for his sons who returned to Judah following the exile, marking him as part of the post-captivity community.
namesAndTitles: The name Arah means 'he wanders' in the original language. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it reflects a personal identity recorded in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Arah as a descendant of Jacob, placing him within the broader covenantal lineage of Israel. Beyond this, the only recorded family relationship is through his sons, who returned to Judah after captivity. No other familial details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Arah's significance lies in his connection to the restoration period of Israel's history. His sons' return to Judah after captivity signifies the preservation and continuation of the Israelite community through generations. This highlights God's faithfulness in sustaining His people despite exile and displacement.
